images.title: Sugarcane pieces in thirds
images.purpose: Pose the question of how many whole sticks are in 4/3 and in 7/3, with the cue that 3 pieces of 1/3 make one whole stick.
images.composition: One reference whole stick at the top, and two loose rows of pieces below it, with wide space between the three rows.
images.exact_structure: Top: one whole sugarcane stick, a plain flat rounded bar, split by thin grey #6B7280 lines into exactly 3 equal pieces. Middle row: exactly 4 loose pieces, each exactly one third of that stick, filled teal #0072B2, evenly spaced. Bottom row: exactly 7 loose pieces of the same size, filled amber #E69F00, evenly spaced. No pieces joined or grouped in either row. Exactly 1 stick, 11 loose pieces.
labels: how many whole sticks in each?
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: Every 3 thirds make one whole stick, so group the pieces in threes.
images.description: A whole stick cut into 3 equal pieces labelled 3/3 = 1 whole stick, above a row of 4 teal thirds labelled 4/3 and a row of 7 amber thirds labelled 7/3.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to circle groups of three pieces in each row and count the groups.

image_decisions.why: A reference stick beside loose thirds gives the grouping cue without grouping the answer.
